page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-288 is a high-density compute and memory instance powered by Intel Xeon 6985P-C processors. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, this virtual machine features 144 physical cores across 288 dedicated vCPUs running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The hardware architecture incorporates a 504 MB shared L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and hardware instruction set extensions including AVX-512, Intel AMX (amx_tile and amx_int8), and cryptographic acceleration via VAES and SHA-NI.

System memory capacity is 2232 GB, providing approximately 7.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. Benchmark results confirm exceptional aggregate memory bandwidth, achieving 1063.61 GB/sec on large-block read operations and 412.0 GB/sec on write operations. Compute benchmarks reflect the substantial parallel capacity of 288 execution threads, registering top-tier results in multi-core stress-ng tests (312050.11), Clang software compilation (70110.0), and PassMark CPU ratings (176858.39). In-memory database evaluations demonstrate high execution capabilities, yielding over 405 million Redis SET operations per second.

Architectural tradeoffs include the absence of dedicated GPUs and bundled local NVMe storage, meaning all persistent storage and network operations rely on remote disk attachments. Additionally, while parallel throughput and multi-threaded scaling are top-tier, single-thread performance falls within standard operational ranges due to the 2.3 GHz base frequency. LLM inference shows viable prompt processing across 7B and 70B parameter models via AMX acceleration, but token generation rates remain limited compared to GPU-backed alternatives.

The c4-highmem-288 configuration is tailored for large-scale enterprise applications requiring significant memory footprints and high parallel processing density. Primary workloads include large in-memory databases like Redis, massive distributed data processing pipelines, enterprise SAP HANA deployments, continuous integration compilation clusters, and extensive matrix-math computational jobs.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-288 is an enterprise compute instance designed for heavy data processing and memory-intensive applications. Built on Intel Xeon 6985P-C processors using the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 288 dedicated vCPUs (144 physical cores) clocked at 2.3 GHz, 504 MB of L3 cache, and 2232 GB of system memory, yielding roughly 7.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware supports advanced instructions such as Intel AMX and AVX-512. The instance contains no bundled local storage or GPUs, relying on network-attached persistent disks. Synthetic benchmarks place this server in the top tier for multi-core compute throughput, clang compilation, and uncached read memory bandwidth exceeding 1060 GB/sec, as well as over 405 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks. Its hardware profile is optimized for in-memory databases, large data analysis, massive build pipelines, and intensive batch workloads.
